name: injection
description: Where untrusted text can become code, a SQL statement, a shell command or markup.

rules.title: eval or exec of a dynamic string
rules.why: eval and exec run whatever text they are given; if any part of it comes from outside, that is code execution.
rules.fix: Parse instead (`ast.literal_eval`, `json`), or look the value up in a table.

rules.title: A shell command through os.system or os.popen
rules.why: The command goes through a shell, so any part of it that came from outside can add commands.
rules.fix: Use `subprocess.run([...])` with a list and no shell.

rules.title: subprocess with shell=True
rules.why: A string run with shell=True is parsed by a shell, so interpolated input can add commands.
rules.fix: Pass the arguments as a list and drop shell=True.

rules.title: A SQL statement built by formatting or concatenation
rules.why: Values spliced into the text of a statement are parsed as SQL, which is how injection works.
rules.fix: Pass values as parameters: `cur.execute("... WHERE id = %s", (value,))`.

match: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id=%s" % uid)
cur.execute("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id=" + uid)

rules.title: A template rendered from a string
rules.why: If any part of the template text comes from outside, the template engine evaluates it.
rules.fix: Render a file template and pass values as variables.

rules.title: eval or new Function on a dynamic string
rules.why: Both run whatever text they are given; if any part of it comes from outside, that is code execution.
rules.fix: Parse the data (`JSON.parse`) or dispatch on a known name.

rules.title: A shell command through child_process.exec
rules.why: exec runs its string in a shell, so a value spliced into it can add commands.
rules.fix: Use `execFile` or `spawn` with an argument array.

rules.title: Markup assigned from a string
rules.why: Markup built from outside text is parsed as markup, so it can carry script.
rules.fix: Set `textContent`, or build nodes, or sanitise with a vetted library.

rules.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML
rules.why: It renders a string as markup, bypassing React's escaping.
rules.fix: Render the text as a child, or sanitise it first with a vetted library.

rules.title: A SQL statement built from a template or concatenation
rules.why: Values spliced into the text of a statement are parsed as SQL.
rules.fix: Use placeholders and pass the values separately.

match: db.query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id=" + id)

rules.title: A command run through a shell
rules.why: A string given to `sh -c` is parsed by a shell, so interpolated input can add commands.
rules.fix: Call the program directly with its arguments as separate strings.

rules.title: A SQL statement built with fmt.Sprintf
rules.why: Values formatted into the statement are parsed as SQL.
rules.fix: Use placeholders and pass the values as arguments.

match: rows, err := db.Query(fmt.Sprintf("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id=%d", id))
db.ExecContext(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("DELETE FROM t WHERE id=%d", id))
clean: db.Query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id=$1", id)

rules.title: A SQL statement built by concatenation
rules.why: Values concatenated into the statement are parsed as SQL, even through prepareStatement.
rules.fix: Use `?` placeholders and bind the values.

match: stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id=" + id)

rules.title: A command run through Runtime.exec
rules.why: A single string is split and run, so interpolated input can change the command.
rules.fix: Use ProcessBuilder with an argument list, and validate what goes into it.

rules.title: A call that runs code or a shell command
rules.why: Each runs its argument as code or as a shell command, so outside input in it is execution.
rules.fix: Avoid them; if a program must run, pass escaped arguments through a fixed command.

rules.title: eval in a shell script
rules.why: eval re-parses its argument as shell code, so a value spliced into it can add commands.
rules.fix: Use arrays and direct invocation instead of building a command string.
